open_issues: Owner decision still needed (spec item 5 / 'expired' certificate): DeviceCertificateBody has no notAfter field. Expiry is still approximated by refusing issuance more than a day ahead plus the optional caller maxAge window (which now applies to the presented leaf only). Adding notAfter later changes the signed body, so it must be settled before the first .wakeel-setup ships.

Owner decision still needed (spec item 2): the printed recovery code is grouped 4-4-4-4-5 (21 characters); the spec text asks for 5 groups of 4, which 21 characters cannot fill. Either 4-4-4-4-4 with the check character shown separately, or the current form.
B7 must be told (spec item 8): PairingQrPayload still carries an extra issuedAt beyond the five listed fields, so the phone can judge the ten minute window from the image alone.

New writer contract for B1/B6: .wakeel-backup, .wakeel-msg, .wakeel-transfer and .wakeel-inventory now REFUSE to be written without ContainerWriteRequest.OrgAgreementPublicKey (the organisation X25519 key that arrives in the setup file). Callers that produce these files must thread that key through, and the administration tool opens them with ContainerKeySource.ForAdmin(orgIdentity).

New pairing contract for B1/B7: PairingAccept.Issue now takes the invitation as a required argument and verifies the request itself, and PairingAcceptBody carries the PC certificate. The phone side should call PairingAccept.EnsureTrusted(orgKey, invitation, revocations, time) rather than assembling the chain by hand.

Desktop host should set ContainerWriteRequest.StagingDirectory and ContainerOpenOptions.StagingDirectory to a folder under C:\ProgramData\Wakeel so container plaintext is never staged in %TEMP% (the handle is self deleting either way).

Signature and stream formats changed while fixing the low findings (labelled signing input for containers, certificates, revocation lists and pairing messages; the AEAD stream header is now authenticated; the manifest gained adminSealedKey). Nothing has shipped, so no migration is needed, but any file produced by the previous build of this package is unreadable by this one.
notes:
Commands run from D:\AI\Administration2 exactly as instructed: `dotnet build src/Wakeel.Crypto && dotnet test tests/Wakeel.Crypto.Tests` — 0 warnings / 0 errors (TreatWarningsAsErrors), Failed 0, Passed 168, Total 168. No package added; Directory.Build.props, Directory.Packages.props and Wakeel.slnx untouched; nothing outside src/Wakeel.Crypto and tests/Wakeel.Crypto.Tests changed; no git command run.

HIGH — ContainerReader chain verification is no longer opt-in. Verification now depends only on VerifyCertificateChain: when it is on (the default) and OrgSigningPublicKey is missing or not 32 bytes, Open throws CryptoException(BadSignature) instead of silently trusting the key inside the producer's own certificate. Skipping the check requires writing VerifyCertificateChain = false. Three tests: opening without the organisation key is refused; a container signed by a self-issued certificate naming the real organisation is refused; the explicit opt-out still opens.

MEDIUM — path escape in ExtractTo. Entry names are now validated the moment the manifest is parsed, with the same rule the write side applies (ContainerEntrySource.IsAcceptableName: no backslash, no "..", no colon, not rooted, no leading slash, no control characters, forward slash sub folders allowed), and duplicates are refused. ExtractTo additionally compares against the root plus a trailing separator, case-insensitively. Test: a re-signed manifest naming "..\\outside\\evil.txt" is refused as Corrupt, plus write-side assertions.

MEDIUM — malformed input now always leaves as CryptoException. UtcInstantConverter.Read uses TryParse and throws JsonException (it also refuses a non-string token), CanonicalJson.Deserialize catches NotSupportedException as well, and ContainerReader.Open validates the manifest shape (producer, producer body, producer signature, entries, every entry's name/sha256/size) before anything reads those fields. Null-body guards were added to DeviceCertificate.VerifySignature, RevocationList.VerifySignature/IsRevoked, CertificateChain.ValidateShape (leaf and issuer), PairingRequest.VerifySignature/VerifyToken/EnsureAcceptable and PairingAccept.VerifySignature/EnsureTrusted. Tests: four malformed instant documents, a manifest with an unreadable date, a manifest whose producer has no body, a manifest that lists nothing.

MEDIUM — PairingAccept.Issue now takes the invitation and calls request.EnsureAcceptable first, so verification cannot be skipped; it also refuses an invitation that does not name the PC certificate's device, and builds the phone certificate body from the PC certificate's OrgId/OfficeId rather than from the request. Tests: issuing for a stray-token request, for an edited request and after the window closed all throw; a further test asserts the issued certificate carries the computer's own office and organisation.

MEDIUM — container staging. Both writer and reader open a single staging file with FileMode.CreateNew + FileOptions.DeleteOnClose (ContainerWriter.CreateStagingFile), the payload is built into it and encrypted straight from the same handle after a seek, and ContainerWriteRequest/ContainerOpenOptions gained StagingDirectory so the host can stage inside ProgramData. Content keys are zeroed in a finally on both sides. Test: staging in a chosen folder round-trips and leaves that folder empty.

MEDIUM — administrator's recovery copy (AGREEMENT item 17 / ARCHITECTURE §4). ContainerManifest gained AdminSealedKey, the writer fills it from ContainerWriteRequest.OrgAgreementPublicKey with label "wakeel.container.adminkey", ContainerKinds.RequiresAdminCopy marks backup/msg/transfer/inventory and the writer refuses those kinds without the organisation key, and ContainerKeySource.ForAdmin(orgIdentity) recovers the content key whatever the payload mode is. Manifest version stays 1. Tests: the organisation opens a password-mode backup and a sealed message, a stranger's identity gets WrongPassword, a backup without the copy is refused (and leaves no .tmp behind), a sync packet offered no organisation key carries no copy.

MEDIUM — phone can now build org→pc→phone from what crosses the cable. PairingAcceptBody carries the PC certificate, and PairingAccept.EnsureTrusted(orgKey, invitation, revocations, time) verifies org→pc, ties that certificate to the QR payload (device id, org, office and X25519 key), checks the accept signature with the certificate's key, checks the answer is not future dated and that the phone certificate matches the named phone, then verifies org→pc→phone. Tests: the whole chain from a serialized invitation plus a serialized accept plus the organisation key only; an answer from an uncertified computer is refused; an answer belonging to another invitation is refused.

LOW — the five byte AEAD stream header (version + declared chunk size) is now part of every frame's associated data; test rewrites the declared chunk size and the stream is refused. LOW — all signatures are domain separated through the new internal DomainSeparation helper ("wakeel.container.sig|v1", "wakeel.cert|v1", "wakeel.revocations|v1", "wakeel.pairing.request|v1", "wakeel.pairing.accept|v1"); test proves a signature over the bare canonical certificate body no longer verifies. LOW — KeyWraps.Expect refuses a wrap whose Salt field disagrees with Kdf.Salt (field kept, so the serialised shape and the spec field list are unchanged). LOW — ContainerWriter.Write(path) writes to path + ".tmp" and moves into place, deleting the temporary on failure. LOW — CertificateChain compares the revocation list's OrgId with the certificate's, refuses a future-dated list, accepts an optional maxRevocationListAge, and passes maxAge: null when recursing into the issuing computer certificate (three new tests plus one proving a freshness window on a phone does not reject an older computer above it). LOW — ReadEntry decrypts the payload once and reads only the requested entry through a hashing stream, and ReadEntries documents that it is for small packets. LOW — Argon2Kdf.DeriveRaw exposes every parameter (including the specification's secret and associated data) and DeriveKey delegates to it; a new test pins the RFC 9106 §5.3 Argon2id vector (32×0x01 password, 16×0x02 salt, 8×0x03 secret, 12×0x04 associated data, m=32 KiB, t=3, p=4) and it matches Konscious 1.3.1 exactly, which also proves the memory cost is counted in kibibytes; a companion test shows the product's own parameters reach the same primitive. B7 must mirror the same vector on Android.
